title: NetSage
summary: A local-first Android network diagnostics workbench combining rule-based log analysis, on-device probes, optional reference-target checks, and evidence-based retesting.
contribution: I independently designed and developed NetSage, including the Android interface, local diagnostic rules, network probes, session storage, report sharing, and test suite.
features: Quick checkup, log diagnosis, and combined diagnosis workflows
On-device network snapshot plus DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP probes
Optional reference-target checks with network-change warnings
Separate IPv4/IPv6 TCP checks with optional three-attempt connection sampling
Top-three hypotheses ranked by evidence strength rather than statistical probability
Matched evidence, conflicting evidence, and step-by-step repair suggestions
Text import, Android share intake, and Markdown or JSON export
Searchable local session history with mode filters and deletion confirmation
Report sharing with an explicit privacy confirmation
Local diagnostic sessions, favorites, and command templates
Offline reference, privacy onboarding, and local persistence
implementation: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose Android client
Versioned local JSON rules with structured observation parsing
Isolated cancellable probes with per-step timeout handling
135 JVM tests passed on 13 October 2026; retained Android 36.1 emulator report records 17 passing tests
Local session persistence plus Android Storage Access Framework import and export
No NetSage server, account, telemetry, or advertising SDK in the v0.2 runtime
limitations: The diagnostic engine is rule-based, not a machine-learning model.
No verified real-user performance metrics are published.
ICMP ping, traceroute, VPN packet capture, cloud synchronization, and background monitoring are outside the verified scope.
